page: Amazon Web Services m7a.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and AMD EPYC 9R14 fourth-generation processors. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The memory subsystem is configured with 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, maintaining the standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio typical of general-purpose instances at 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes hardware support for vector extensions like AVX-512, cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI, and advanced bit manipulation instructions. It does not bundle any local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs, instead relying on networked storage infrastructure and providing a 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput across heavily parallelized workloads. The m7a.24xlarge scores in the top tier for multi-core stress-ng tests (293,589.22) and Geekbench multi-core performance (22,335.0), with particularly strong marks in PassMark CPU tests (106,240.69) and Clang software compilation (77,991.0). Single-threaded tasks remain solid, categorized in the top 25% with a 3,075.97 stress-ng rating and a 1,987.0 Geekbench single-core score. In caching and memory bandwidth benchmarks, the server registers 11,726.96 GB/sec on small cached blocks, while sustaining 328.46 GB/sec read and 159.69 GB/sec write on larger uncached blocks. In-memory operations are equally competitive, achieving 168.46 million Redis SET operations per second and strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the m7a.24xlarge balances high-density computational throughput with broad general-purpose utility. The dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores eliminate cross-thread resource contention, making it an efficient allocation for high-concurrency environments without sacrificing deterministic processing latency. However, the total absence of direct-attached local storage necessitates reliance on external network volumes, making network bandwidth a critical factor for I/O-intensive workloads. Given its 96-core density, 384 GB DDR5 allocation, and 38 Gbps baseline network capacity, this instance is well suited for enterprise database clusters, parallel code compilation pipelines, in-memory caches, large-scale web serving tiers, and distributed data processing frameworks.
